target: Vuelvo a casa en metro.
english: I go back home by metro.
tip: 'A casa' with no article means 'home', not 'to a house'. Bare 'casa' = your own home: 'vuelvo a casa' = I head home.

target: Termino de trabajar a las seis.
english: I finish working at six.
tip: 'Termino trabajando' exists but means 'I end up working'. To finish doing something, Spanish needs de + infinitive: 'termino de trabajar' = I finish working.

target: Él se afeita cada dos días.
english: He shaves every other day.
tip: 'Cada dos días' is literally 'each two days' – that's how Spanish says 'every other day'. No word for 'other' needed: you count the interval instead.

target: Me acuerdo perfectamente de ese día.
english: I remember that day perfectly.
tip: "Acordarse de" = to remember. Always reflexive + de: "Me acuerdo de ese día." Without "de" is a common mistake.

target: El mapa está en la mochila.
english: The map is in the backpack.
tip: "El mapa" is masculine. Not all -a nouns are feminine – mapa is an exception to memorize.

target: Me interesan las ofertas de empleo.
english: Job offers interest me.
tip: Interesar: me interesan (plural) – agrees with 'las ofertas'.

target: Faltan nueve días para las vacaciones.
english: There are nine days until the vacation.
tip: Vacation is always plural in Spanish: 'las vacaciones'. Even one trip takes plural articles and verbs – mis vacaciones fueron cortas.

target: El problema es que no tengo tiempo.
english: The problem is I don't have time.
tip: "El problema" is masculine. Many -ma words from Greek are masculine: problema, tema, sistema, programa, clima, idioma.

target: El ferry tardó tres horas en llegar.
english: The ferry took three hours to arrive.
tip: Taking time is 'tardar EN': 'tardó tres horas en llegar' = lit. delayed three hours in arriving. English 'to arrive' tempts you toward 'a' – it's always en.

target: Me desperté tarde y perdí el desayuno.
english: I woke up late and missed breakfast.
tip: No verb 'to miss' needed: 'perdí el desayuno' – perder means lose AND miss. You 'lose' buses, flights and breakfasts in Spanish.

target: Se despidió de todos antes de irse.
english: He said goodbye to everyone before leaving.
tip: Despedir = to fire someone; add se and it means to say goodbye. 'Se despidió de todos' = he said goodbye to everyone – and that 'de' is mandatory.

target: Brindamos por los novios.
english: We toasted to the couple.
tip: "Por" = for the sake of / in honor of: "Brindamos por tu éxito."

target: La moto está aparcada fuera.
english: The motorcycle is parked outside.
tip: "La moto" – feminine because it's short for "la motocicleta." Keeps gender of the full word.

target: Me parece bien tu idea.
english: Your idea sounds good to me.
tip: Tu idea is the subject and the opinion-holder is just an object: me. Where English reaches for 'I think it's good', Spanish prefers me parece bien – it seems-good to me.

target: Imprimí veinte copias del informe.
english: I printed twenty copies of the report.
tip: 'Del' is the mandatory contraction of 'de + el': never write 'de el'. 'De la' stays separate (no contraction for feminine).

target: En abril suele llover bastante.
english: In April it usually rains quite a bit.
tip: 'Usually' isn't an adverb here – it's the verb 'suele'. Spanish conjugates soler + infinitive for habits: 'suele llover' = it tends-to rain.

target: ¿Te apetece ir a tomar algo?
english: Do you feel like going for a drink?
tip: 'Tomar algo' isn't 'take something' – it's the standard invite for going out for a drink. Tomar covers eating and drinking: tomar un café, una caña.

target: Me cae muy bien tu amigo.
english: I really like your friend (as a person).
tip: Never say 'me gusta tu amigo' unless you fancy him – gustar with people can sound romantic. For plain liking, use 'me cae bien': he 'falls well' on you.

target: Si no lloviera, iríamos al parque.
english: If it weren't raining, we would go to the park.
tip: English fakes a past tense for unreal ifs ('if it weren't'); Spanish has a dedicated form. 'Si no llovía' is wrong – an unreal si needs lloviera, paired with iríamos.

target: Le da vergüenza hablar en público.
english: He's embarrassed to speak in public.
tip: Spanish doesn't say he IS embarrassed – public speaking gives him shame: le da vergüenza. Emotions here are things that hit you, not things you are.

target: Todavía nos quedan cosas por hacer.
english: We still have things left to do.
tip: "Por" + infinitive = still to be done: "Queda mucho por hacer" = There's a lot left to do.

target: Te llamé por teléfono tres veces.
english: I called you by phone three times.
tip: "Por" = via / by means of: "Lo dije por teléfono." Por for the method of communication.

target: La vi ayer en el supermercado.
english: I saw her yesterday at the supermarket.
tip: 'Her' shrinks to one syllable BEFORE the verb: 'La vi' = her I-saw. English order (vi la) is flat-out wrong – object pronouns latch on in front.

target: Este plato lleva tomate, cebolla y pimiento.
english: This dish has tomato, onion, and bell pepper.
tip: Dishes 'carry' their ingredients: 'lleva tomate' = it has tomato in it. Ask '¿qué lleva?' in any restaurant to hear what's inside a dish.

target: No hay nadie que sepa la respuesta.
english: There's nobody who knows the answer.
tip: Sepa, not sabe: after no hay nadie que..., that person doesn't exist, so Spanish switches to subjunctive. Nonexistent people don't get real-world verb forms.

target: Caminamos por el casco antiguo toda la tarde.
english: We walked through the old town all afternoon.
tip: "Por" for movement through a place. "Caminamos por" = we walked through/around.

target: La radio está muy alta, bájala un poco.
english: The radio is too loud, turn it down a bit.
tip: La radio – feminine in Spain. Can be el radio in some Latin American countries.

target: Pasamos la Navidad en casa de los abuelos.
english: We spent Christmas at the grandparents' house.
tip: En casa de = at someone's house (no article needed).

target: Me pidió disculpas por el malentendido de ayer.
english: He apologized to me for yesterday's misunderstanding.
tip: Spanish apologizes by asking: 'pidió disculpas' = requested pardons. You ask for forgiveness rather than offer an apology.

target: El museo está al final de esta avenida.
english: The museum is at the end of this avenue.
tip: 'Al' is the mandatory contraction of 'a + el': 'al parque', 'al cine'. It only happens with masculine singular 'el'.
